parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module groups infrastructure adapters together: in-memory repositories, Express controllers and the server.ts composition root. That is a normal grouping for an infrastructure layer, not a split into unrelated concerns. However, the rule for mapping errors to HTTP responses lives in two places. OrderController has a private handleError method that maps errors to 400/404/500 responses with an { error } body. ProductController.listAll repeats the same 500 fallback branches inline instead of sharing that logic, so a change to error statuses or the response format must be made in two places. handleError also matches domain errors by comparing hard-coded name strings instead of using the error classes. There is smaller repetition inside files too: InMemoryOrderRepository repeats the order copy expression in four methods, and OrderController repeats the route-parameter unwrapping three times. The duplicated error-mapping rule matches the rubric's fail condition.

violations.message: ProductController.listAll repeats the error-to-HTTP response rule (500 { error } fallbacks) instead of sharing OrderController.handleError, so this rule now lives in two places.
handleError is a private method, so other controllers can't share the error-to-status mapping, and it identifies domain errors by hard-coded name strings instead of their error classes.
